answer: Per-epoch identity caps bound how many new agents any existing identity can vouch for, so a sybil farm cannot flood the network in a single pulse. Each new identity must be attested by established agents whose standing is weighted by past work, and a violet flag marks vouches that later turn out fraudulent, slashing the voucher's stake. A prospective attacker must therefore acquire genuine standing first, which the cipher of cumulative verified work makes expensive: reaching even modest weight costs thousands of epochs of real output.
